chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ali al-Sa'igh, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, and I was present, about a man who began with Al-Marwa before Al-Safa. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should repeat. Do you not see that if he had begun with his left before his right, he would be required to begin with his right, then return to his left?'

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa (the first hill in the Sa'i ritual)
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwa (the second hill in the Sa'i ritual)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim starts Sa'i with Marwa before Safa?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who erroneously begins Sa'i with Marwa, ruling that the act must be repeated entirely. The Imam employs a logical analogy from ritual purity (wudu), where starting with the left hand necessitates correcting the sequence by performing the right side first and then returning to the left, thereby establishing the principle of restoring the proper order through repetition rather than mere completion. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the prescribed sequence (tartib) as an integral component of the ritual's validity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Ali Al Sani’e who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked and I was present, about a man who began with Al-Marwa before Al-Safa. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should repeat. Do you not see that had he began (his ablution) with his left hand before his right hand, upon him would be that he begins with his right hand, then return upon his left hand?’
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Isma‘il ibn Marrar from Yunus from Ali al-Sa‘igh who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked, when I was present, about a man who begins from al- Marwah instead of from al-Safa’. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must do it again. Consider if you begin with your left arms for wudu’ instead of with your right arm, you must begin with your right arm and then do your left arm again.’”
